description: A person or entity, as a circular image. Static: it is a picture, not a control.

curated.by: read from @adobe/spectrum-wc 2.0.0-beta.6 (dist/components/avatar/avatar.js, the css`` template) and its shipped type declarations; the design file was used to check the result, not to derive it

figma.notes: Component set on page "Avatar". The set's Style axis offers four placeholder treatments — a photo, a generated gradient, initials and a guest glyph. Only the photo exists in the implementation; the rest are sample content drawn in the file. See a-style-axis.

props.name: size
props.notes: Seventeen rungs. The design file labels each with its pixel box, 50 (16x16); the code value is the rung alone.

props.name: src
props.notes: URL of the image. The design file has no counterpart: it draws sample content instead.

props.name: alt
props.notes: Describes the person or entity. An empty string marks the image decorative and hides it from assistive technology.

props.name: outline
props.notes: A ring around the image, for avatars that overlap or sit on a busy ground.

props.name: decorative
props.notes: Hides the image from assistive technology without clearing alt.

states.name: disabled
states.notes: Dims the image and stops pointer events. Not an interactive state: the avatar is static.

composition.name: .Gradient image
composition.why: Sample content drawn in the design file for the Gradient image style. The implementation renders whatever src points at, so there is nothing to contract.

composition.name: .Gradient background
composition.why: The same, for the gradient's backing fill.

composition.name: .S2_Icon_Avatar_20_Filled
composition.why: The guest placeholder glyph, from the icon rig. Also sample content rather than anatomy.

slot.name: image
slot.notes: The picture itself, from src. The design file fills it with a sample photo, exported alongside so a preview has something real to draw rather than an empty circle.

notes: An image, not a control. It renders and takes no focus.
alt describes the person or entity; alt="" or decorative marks it decorative and hides it from assistive technology.
Disabled dims the image; it conveys no state to assistive technology because the avatar is not interactive.

decisions.question: The first contract for this component was scaffolded from the design file and described a row of six boxes.
decisions.chose: Rebuilt from the implementation, as badge, button and icon were
decisions.decision: The real component is a sized circle and an image, twenty-four CSS rules in total. The scaffolder had transcribed the design file's node tree — the gradient artwork, the initials text, the guest glyph and the stroke — as anatomy, laid them out as flex siblings, and hid none of them, so the preview drew six boxes side by side.
decisions.evidence: dist/components/avatar/avatar.js is 2,193 bytes; the scaffolded contract was roughly 900 lines with 327 refusals.

decisions.question: The design file has a Style axis with four values — User image, Gradient image, Initials, Guest — and the implementation has no such property.
decisions.chose: Left it out of props and recorded it here
decisions.fix: Ask the Spectrum team whether the generated gradient, the initials and the guest glyph are meant to ship. Today an avatar renders whatever src points at and nothing else, so a consumer wanting initials has to draw them.
decisions.evidence: Avatar.base.d.ts declares src, alt, size, outline, disabled and decorative. There is no style property, and avatar.js renders one .

decisions.question: The design labels each size with its pixel box; the code uses the rung alone.
decisions.chose: The contract carries the code value and maps to the design label
decisions.decision: size is "500" in code and "500 (40x40)" in the file. The value map in the size prop is the translation.
decisions.evidence: AVATAR_VALID_SIZES is a numeric tuple; the Figma Size axis carries the labels.

decisions.question: An avatar with no src is an empty circle, so the preview had nothing to show.
decisions.chose: Export the design's own placeholder photo into the package and name it on the slot
decisions.decision: The sample is the design file's art, not something invented. It is a slot default, so it describes what the design puts there; it is never a value the component ships with.
decisions.fix: The schema has no key for a media slot's sample art, so it is recorded under default.props, whose description covers the design's overrides on the instance. A `sample` key would read better.
decisions.evidence: exported from the Size=1400 User image variant's Photo layer.

decisions.question: The renderer had no way to emit an image whose src is a prop, so the preview drew a placeholder comment.
decisions.chose: Declared the image part as an asset whose prop is the source
decisions.decision: The asset form already emitted , but required a manifest and field because it was built for lookup tables like the product icons. An avatar has no key to resolve: src is the source. Those two fields are now optional.
decisions.evidence: The slot is kept alongside: it records what the design fills the picture with, including the exported sample.

decisions.question: Toggling outline changed nothing in the preview.
decisions.chose: Declare the attribute the styling keys on
decisions.decision: The image's outline rule is written against [data-outline="true"], and the prop declared no attr, so the generated component never set one. A prop that conditions styling has to name the attribute that carries it.
decisions.evidence: The rendered root carried data-size and data-disabled but no data-outline, so the rule could not match.
